steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Quality control (QC) inspects the finished product to detect defects - it's reactive and occurs after production. Defective items are rejected or reworked. | Key Fact: Quality assurance (QA) builds quality into every stage of the production process - it's proactive and aims to prevent defects before they occur. | Key Fact: Total quality management (TQM) involves every employee in continuous quality improvement: zero defects culture, employee empowerment, and customer focus throughout the organisation. | Key Fact: ISO 9001 is an international quality standard: businesses must document processes, demonstrate consistent quality, and pass regular audits. Certification builds customer trust.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain the difference between quality control and quality assurance. | Describe two ways TQM can benefit a business. | Evaluate whether a small business should invest in ISO 9001 certification.
